_note: Massachusetts move-in-charge and fee rules, quoted verbatim from M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B on malegislature.gov and 940 CMR 3.17 (the Attorney General's c. 93A landlord-tenant regulation) on mass.gov, both retrieved 2026-06-20. § 15B(1)(b) is an exhaustive list of the only four lawful up-front charges (first month, last month, a one-month security deposit, and the cost of a key and lock) — there is no lawful application, screening, move-in, amenity, or pet up-front fee. § 15B(1)(c) bars any interest or penalty for late rent until 30 days after it was due; 940 CMR 3.17(6)(a) restates that bar. status=draft-unverified: must be reviewed by a Massachusetts tenant attorney / legal-aid clinic before public conclusions.

rules.title: Late fee charged before rent is 30 days overdue
rules.description: Per M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(c), no lease may impose interest or a penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after the rent was due. The Attorney General's regulation 940 CMR 3.17(6)(a) makes charging such a late fee earlier an unfair or deceptive practice. A clause imposing a late fee on day 1, day 5, or any time inside the 30-day window is unenforceable.
rules.tenant_explainer: Massachusetts landlords can't charge a late fee until your rent is a full 30 days overdue. A 'late fee after 5 days' or '$50 if rent is late' clause isn't enforceable here.

citations.label: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(c)
citations.quote: No lease or other rental agreement shall impose any interest or penalty for failure to pay rent until thirty days after such rent shall have been due.

citations.label: 940 CMR 3.17(6)(a)
citations.quote: It shall be an unfair and deceptive practice for an owner to: (a) Impose any interest or penalty for late payment or rent unless such payment is 30 days overdue;

rules.title: Application or tenant-screening fee charged up front
rules.description: Per M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), the only amounts a lessor may require at or before the start of a tenancy are first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit equal to one month's rent, and the cost of a new key and lock. 940 CMR 3.17(4)(a) restates this exhaustive list. An application fee, screening fee, or credit-check fee is not on that list and is an unlawful up-front charge.
rules.tenant_explainer: In Massachusetts a landlord can only collect four things before you move in: first month, last month, a one-month security deposit, and the cost of a new lock and key. An application fee or credit-check fee isn't allowed.

citations.label: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b)
citations.quote: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following: (i) rent for the first full month of occupancy; and, (ii) rent for the last full month of occupancy calculated at the same rate as the first month; and, (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent

citations.label: 940 CMR 3.17(4)(a)
citations.quote: It shall be an unfair or deceptive practice for an owner to: (a) require a tenant or prospective tenant, at or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, to pay any amount in excess of the following:

rules.title: Move-in, amenity, pet, or other up-front fee not allowed by statute
rules.description: Per M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b), the up-front charges a lessor may require are exhaustively limited to first month's rent, last month's rent, a one-month security deposit, and the cost of a key and lock. A move-in fee, amenity fee, redecorating fee, community fee, or non-refundable pet fee charged at or before move-in is outside that list and is an unlawful up-front charge.
rules.tenant_explainer: Beyond first month, last month, a one-month deposit, and the cost of a lock and key, Massachusetts landlords can't charge extra up-front fees — no move-in fee, pet fee, or amenity fee before you move in.

citations.label: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b)(iv)
citations.quote: (iv) the purchase and installation cost for a key and lock.

citations.label: M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(d)
citations.quote: No lessor or successor in interest shall at any time subsequent to the commencement of a tenancy demand rent in advance in excess of the current month's rent or a security deposit in excess of the amount allowed by this section.
